brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Two full hex bases (piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0) form the body, with a top cover on the first base.
Bin hex-bin-full-div3 (full depth, 3 compartments) seated in cell 0,0,0. It drops in and hangs on its rim, so it is removable.
Notch drawer frame hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at cell 0,1,0, filling the gap between the two bases. The frame is placed; I did not separately add a drawer box part.
Handle handle:0,0,0;top on the top cover, with three inserts seating it.
Build is compact (9 parts) and handle-carried, but this checks fit only; I did not verify weight or strength.

finish.summary: Built a small organizer: two hex bases, a 3-compartment removable bin, a notch drawer frame between the bases, and a top grab handle on a cover. check_build reports meshClash clear with no rule errors (only an info note about open cap faces, which are optional). Drawer frame is the only drawer-type part available at this placement; its pull-out drawer element was not separately confirmed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
